title: [Characteristics of Patients with Digital Health Applications for Mental Disorders - Analysis results of insured persons in Rhineland Palatinate/Saarland].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insured patients with a prescription for a digital health application for mental disorders (PsyDiGA) receive an activation code from their health insurance. We examined characteristics of insured persons receiving and redeeming an activation code.
METHODS: Billing data of insured adults with mental disorders from AOK Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland in 2020-2022 were analysed using logistic regression models.
RESULTS: The sample for the analysis comprised 280,706 insured persons: 280,103 insured persons without an activation code and 603 insured persons with one (of whom 457 had redeemed theirs). Female patients, patients younger than 35 years as well as those with depressive, anxiety or sleep disorders were more likely to receive an activation code (e. g. odds ratio (OR) female vs. male 1.32, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-1.57; depressive vs. other disorder adjusted OR 2.36 (95% CI 1.94-2.89)). Patients aged 35-44 years were less likely to redeem an activation code compared to those aged 25-34 years (OR 0.46, 95%-CI 0.27-0.78).
DISCUSSION: Our PsyDiGA results based on data from the AOK align with other insurance companies reporting that DiGA are prescribed primarily to women and younger people.
CONCLUSION: Before prescribing a PsyDiGA in case of a suitable indication, especially to persons aged 35-44 years, physicians and psychotherapists should discuss with their patients whether PsyDiGA can be integrated into their daily routine.
